overview: The Centre of Excellence for Robotics (CoER) is a specialized initiative under the Department of Science & Technology (DST) aimed at advancing robotics and automation technologies in India. It focuses on fostering innovation, research, and development in strategic areas such as deep technologies, including robotics, to strengthen national capabilities and promote technological self-reliance. The scheme supports private sector participation and aligns with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision by encouraging indigenization in critical sectors.
objectives: Encourage private sector involvement in high-impact R&D
Promote strategic technologies including robotics and deep technologies
Foster self-reliance and economic security through indigenization
Ensure flexibility in sectoral support for public interest
Strengthen India’s capabilities in strategic technologies for global competitiveness
Support technologies where indigenization is essential for strategic or economic reasons
Allow support for additional sectors or technologies deemed essential for public interest
eligibility: Eligible Technology Entities means any legal entity which is engaged in developing RDI-intensive technology (TRL4 and above). These could include companies registered under the Companies Act 2013, partnerships registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and limited liability partnerships registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, engaged in scale-up of RDI-intensive technologies beyond Technology Readiness Level 4. These shall include startups as defined in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade Notification G.S.R. 127(E) dated 19 February 2019, as may be modified from time to time.
benefits: Funding can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative RDI projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above; exceptions may be approved by the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Financial support includes long-term loans at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion (especially for startups), and contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Grants and short-term loans are not supported. Ownership of physical and intellectual property created or acquired out of RDIF funds vests with Eligible Technology Entities.
financial_support: Total Budget: ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of Financing: Long-term loan at low or nil interest rates. Equity infusion, especially in case of startups. Contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Exclusions: Grants and short-term loans are not supported. Coverage: Financing can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative RDI projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above; exceptions may be approved by the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS).
application_process: Industry stakeholders seeking funding for projects under the RDI scheme are requested not to send proposals or emails directly to DST. All disbursements will be routed exclusively through the designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs) in due course through separate advertisement. Interested Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs) are invited to express their interest in partnering with this fund by writing to Dr Jyoti Sharma, Head, RDI Cell at sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in. Existing NBFCs planning to establish AIFs are also encouraged to contact the Department of Science & Technology (DST) regarding potential participation. For more details visit: https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/
implementing_agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology
caveats: Grants and short-term loans are not supported under the RDI scheme
Funding is routed exclusively through Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs); direct applications to DST are not accepted
RDIF shall have to return the entire fund to the Consolidated Fund of India only after 50 years, without any interest
